title: Beyond VRAM Capacity: A Single-Workstation Case Study of Strata, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and OpenCode on an RTX 5080
description:
Verified single-workstation systems case study of OCF V1 (OpenCode FlashNext) by Arun C Michael. Documents hybrid memory placement, client compaction control, and single-slot FIFO orchestration that runs an 83.62 GB on-disk IQ3_S sparse coding model (ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF) on an NVIDIA RTX 5080 (16 GB) with Strata and OpenCode.

Key verified findings include: direct-NVMe PLE placement saving ~26.8 GiB host RAM; wire-verified non-reasoning compaction reducing paired-fixture latency from 69.282 s to 18.360 s (−73.5%); MTP draft acceptance ~73.49%; and deterministic 600 s idle unload with ~30.515 s cold wake. Includes sanitized configs, scripts, claims ledger, and the PDF whitepaper asset from GitHub release v1.0.0.

Release v1.2.0 adds full retained all-workspace token economics for 3–8 November 2026: 5,290,865 OpenCode output tokens (5,090,841 coding + 200,024 compaction) across 224 coding sessions, with cache-read tokens (373,320,427) dominating 94.79% of recorded input against 20,537,861 fresh-input tokens. The same recorded footprint priced at published list rates yields a cloud counterfactual band of $8.43–$259.48 ($275.13 for a Teams-plus-CTR case), versus a $0 local API charge; electricity figures are illustrative assumptions, not measurements. Counterfactuals are not invoices, meters are non-additive, and no quality parity is claimed.

Do not redistribute GGUF weights from this archive—fetch and verify shards from the upstream Hugging Face repository.
